name: Van Buren State Park Hiking Trails
description: System of 9 named hiking loops within Van Buren State Park. Hikers are also permitted on the mountain biking and bridle trails.
identity_notes: Named loops: Green Trail (1 mi), Blue Trail (2 mi), Orange Trail (2 mi), Haiku Trail (0.2 mi), Sensory Trail (0.1 mi), Pink Trail (4 mi), Red Trail (2 mi), White Trail (1 mi), Yellow Trail (2 mi). Trailhead at south side parking lot. These named loops likely qualify as Trail Segments; resolve in normalization. Van Buren State Park Map (downloadable) available — may contain segment geometry. Map rev. 10/2025 shows corrected loop lengths: Pink=2.6mi, White=1.5mi, Orange=1.0mi. Purple Trail (0.3mi Easy) also documented on map — previously missing. Campground Connector (0.1mi Mod), Day Use Connector (0.1mi Easy), Cable Line Road Trail also shown. Sensory Trail (0.2mi) appears on map body.

name: Van Buren State Park Mountain Bike Trails
description: Three miles of mostly single-track mountain bike trails meander through the south shore woods providing both novice and intermediate riders with scenic views of Van Buren woodlands while crossing the boardwalks over ravines and offering some challenging features.
identity_notes: Named loops: Green Trail (1 mi), Blue Trail (2 mi). Hikers also permitted. Trailhead at South Shore Picnic Area parking lot.

name: Van Buren State Park Bridle Trails
identity_notes: Named loops: Red Trail (2 mi), Pink Trail (4 mi), White Trail (1 mi), Yellow Trail (2 mi). Trailhead at day-use bridle area. Baseline listed "Van Buren Bridle Trail" — confirmed. Overnight Bridle Camp not confirmed on current page; verify via ODNR reservation system. Length/difficulty from official ODNR park map rev. 10/2025 — supersedes ODNR web page text.

name: Heritage Trail
identity_notes: HPD website lists 16 numbered segments totaling 20.22 miles. Trail passes through Litzenberg Memorial Woods, Indian Green-Worden CA, Liberty Landing, Blanchard River Greenway, Great Karg Well, Riverwalk, Eastpoint Area, Riverbend Recreation Area, and connecting road/trail corridors. Stage 16 Trail Segment records separately.

name: Blanchard River Water Trail
identity_notes: ODNR-designated water trail, HPD-managed (per §4.6 management tier governs — T3 entity, not T2). Begins at Blanchard River Nature Preserve (22006 CR 17, Forest — COUNTY_VERIFY: may be Hardin County), ends at Blanchard Landing (SR 235 S of US 224 W, Findlay — Hancock). If start is in Hardin County, CROSS_COUNTY_CANDIDATE for Hancock + Hardin. Access points: Blanchard River NP (start), Jackson Landing, Riverbend Recreation Area (primitive campground), Waterfalls Area (portage), Great Karg Well (portage), Liberty Landing (9.3mi float start), Blanchard Landing (end). Downstream of Blanchard Landing continues to Putnam County (not part of designated BRWT).

name: Blanchard River Greenway Trail
identity_notes: Urban greenway linking parks and downtown Findlay. Route: Bright Road (eastern terminus at Eastpoint Area) to Fox Street (western terminus at River Landings), with connection to Broad Avenue and Township Road 89. Passes through seven River Parks: Eastpoint Area, Waterfalls Area, Riverside Park Waterfront (T6 — City of Findlay), Centennial Park, Great Karg Well Historical Site, River Landings, and HPD Administrative Offices. Riverside Park Waterfront is no longer HPD-managed (agreement ended Jan 1 2026) — will be T6 entity.

name: Riverwalk
identity_notes: Owned by City of Findlay, managed by HPD (since 1987) — T3 per §4.6. Route: Anchor Park to Cory Street along south side of Blanchard River. Part of Heritage Trail route (segment 7 passes through Riverwalk). Original development won 1989 OPRA Outstanding Facility Award. Redevelopment planned (aging infrastructure noted on page).

name: Highline Trail

name: Bluffton Bicycle Pathway
identity_notes: CROSS_COUNTY_CANDIDATE — Also called "Village of Bluffton Pathway" (American Trails). Pathway connects Buckeye Park (400 W. Trailhead-specific GPS to be confirmed during GPS Acquisition Module pass.

name: Findlay Reservoir Dike Trail
governance: City of Findlay — Water Department; Ohio Department of Natural Resources Division of Wildlife (cooperative management)
identity_notes: T6 MISS — found during T8 discovery pass 2026-05-15. Earthen dike trail surrounding Findlay Reservoirs #1 and #2 (City of Findlay municipal water supply). Reservoir #1 dike = 2.0 miles; Reservoir #2 dike = 4.3 miles; shared dike between reservoirs = 1.0 mile; outer perimeter of combined reservoir system = 5.3 miles (source: hiking-ohio.com). Trail on City of Findlay earthen infrastructure dikes; ODNR cooperative agreement covers recreation access. Notable as eBird hotspot L285907 (Findlay Reservoirs) — popular winter waterfowl birding. Often described in conjunction with Riverbend Recreation Area (HPD T3) — physically adjacent but distinct governance. Staged at discovery_tier=6 (City of Findlay). GPS pending GPS Acquisition Module pass. Seeded from Copilot baseline (Findlay Reservoir Trail).
